title: Spark reclassifies abstention from a neutral third option into a rationed exception requiring pre-disclosed conflict
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.3.3 requires a Delegate to "cast a vote (For / Against) on 100% of governance proposals within the designated voting window." A.6.1.1.1.3.1.3.3.4 restricts Abstain to "solely... cases where the Delegate has a documented conflict of interest for the specific proposal," the conflict must be disclosed *before* the voting window opens (.3.4.1), and .3.4.2 states flatly that "abstaining for any reason other than a disclosed conflict is treated as non-performance."

This inverts the usual treatment of abstention. In most voting systems abstaining is the costless default — the safe move for a delegate who is uninformed, uncertain, or unwilling to alienate anyone. Spark makes it the *most* expensive option: it requires an advance filing, is only available on grounds of conflict, and otherwise counts toward removal.

The target is delegate free-riding. A paid delegate who abstains on contested proposals collects compensation while taking no position, produces no signal for delegators to evaluate, and cannot be held to any record. Forcing a binary choice plus a written rationale (.3.3.5) means every delegate accumulates a reviewable voting history.

The risk accepted in exchange is coerced votes on proposals a delegate genuinely does not understand. The framework's implicit answer is that an ill-considered recorded vote is more accountable than a silence, because a bad record can be judged and silence cannot.
description: Delegates must vote For or Against on 100% of proposals; Abstain is valid only for a conflict disclosed before the voting window, and abstaining otherwise counts as non-performance.
